title: See the road with rays
summary: A brain only knows what its inputs tell it. Give it better eyes and watch what changes.

steps.title: Pick a harder road
steps.body:
The Oval is gentle, so almost any brain gets round it. To see what inputs are worth, train on the Hairpin instead.

Add an `each generation` block at the bottom. It runs once between generations, after every car has stopped. Inside it, `useTrack(id: "hairpin")` picks the road.

The editor will note that some evolution settings now use their defaults. That is fine. Lesson 5 is all about them.

check.message: Add an each generation block that calls useTrack(id: "hairpin").

hints: Blocks look like each tick { ... }. This one is each generation { ... }.
At the bottom, write each generation { useTrack(id: "hairpin") } on three lines.

steps.title: One eye is not enough
steps.body:
The starter swapped in `racing-tiny`. It has two inputs: one ray straight ahead and the speed.

Press Check to train it for 10 generations. With a single ray the brain cannot tell which way the road bends or how close it is to either edge, and the Hairpin catches it every time.

Inputs are numbers from sensors, and they are everything a brain knows about the world. Switch back to `racing-starter` and check again.

check.message: Training should get the best car past 300 m on the Hairpin.

hints: The brain line picks which inputs the network gets.
Change brain racing-tiny to brain racing-starter.

steps.title: Build your own sensor
steps.body:
A `sensor` line adds one more input to the brain. Give it a name, a label, a range and a value.

Brains work best with inputs between 0 and 1, so the range tells the app how to squeeze the value. With `-90 deg .. 90 deg`, a car pointing 90 degrees right reads 0, a car pointing straight down the road reads 0.5, and 90 degrees left reads 1.

Add a sensor that reads `car.headingError`, the angle between the car and the road. A sensor changes the shape of the brain, so a run that is already training has to start a new branch.

check.message: The brain should have 5 inputs: three rays, the speed and your sensor.

hints: The pattern is sensor name "Label" in low .. high = value.
Add sensor heading "Heading error" in -90 deg .. 90 deg = car.headingError below the brain line.

steps.title: Nine rays and a compass
steps.body:
`racing-standard` has nine rays, the speed and the heading error built in. With it, your sensor would be a copy of an input the brain already has, so remove it.

More inputs let a brain see more, but each one adds weights that evolution has to tune. Bigger brains often need more generations before they pay off.

Switch to `racing-standard` and delete your sensor.

check.message: The brain should have 11 inputs: nine rays, the speed and the heading error.

hints: Two changes: the brain line, and the sensor lines go away.
Use brain racing-standard and delete the sensor heading line and its comment.
